airplane: Airplanes appear as elongated metallic objects with distinct fuselage, wings, and tail, parked on hardstand areas or taxiways. They differ from airports by being discrete aircraft rather than the entire aviation facility with runways and terminals; runways show linear pavement markings without aircraft shape; meadows show open grassy areas without any metallic structures.
airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and aircraft parking stands. They differ from runways by including terminal buildings and parking areas rather than just pavement; industrial areas show factories and smokestacks rather than aviation infrastructure; parking lots show vehicle rows without runways or aircraft.
baseball_diamond: Baseball diamonds show diamond-shaped infields with visible pitcher's mound, baselines, outfield grass, and surrounding fences. They differ from golf courses by having sports diamond geometry rather than fairways and bunkers; stadiums have large surrounding stands and enclosed seating; ground track fields show oval running tracks rather than diamond infields.
basketball_court: Basketball courts show rectangular paved areas with clear court markings, center circle, and key areas, often with surrounding fences. They differ from tennis courts by having different court markings and key areas rather than net lines; mobile home parks show trailer units rather than sports courts; parking lots have vehicle rows rather than court markings.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors, wave patterns, and occasional beach umbrellas. They contrast with islands by being coastal shorelines rather than land surrounded by water; deserts lack water adjacency and wave patterns; sea ice shows frozen white surfaces rather than sandy shores.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars, deck, and approach ramps. They differ from harbors by being crossing structures rather than waterfront facilities with docks and ships; rivers show water channels without bridges; freeways are ground-level corridors without span structures.
chaparral: Chaparral appears as dense, low, dark-green shrub vegetation with irregular edges covering hillsides, showing rough texture. It contrasts with deserts by having dense vegetation cover rather than sand dunes; forests have taller tree canopy rather than low shrubs; mountains show exposed rock and elevation rather than uniform shrub cover.
church: Churches show distinctive religious architecture with prominent spires, steeples, or domes, often with a central nave and surrounding parking. They differ from palaces by having religious spires rather than ornate palace architecture; sparse residential shows housing units without religious structures; commercial areas show retail buildings and signage rather than churches.
circular_farmland: Circular farmland shows large pivot-irrigated fields with concentric circular patterns, visible center-pivot systems, and uniform crop rings. It differs from rectangular farmland by having circular geometry rather than straight field boundaries; storage tanks show metallic circular containers rather than crop circles; terraces show stepped agricultural patterns on slopes.
cloud: Clouds appear as bright white to gray irregular masses with soft edges, diffuse boundaries, and varying textures in the sky. They differ from mountains by lacking solid ground and elevation contours; sea ice shows frozen surface patterns rather than atmospheric formations; chaparral shows vegetation on ground rather than sky phenomena.
commercial_area: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts or signage. They contrast with industrial areas by having retail stores rather than warehouses and smokestacks; palaces show ornate architecture rather than commercial blocks; dense residential shows housing units rather than commercial buildings.
dense_residential: Dense residential features tightly packed housing units with small yards, narrow streets, and uniform block patterns. It differs from medium residential by having smaller lot sizes and less green space; mobile home parks show narrow trailer units rather than houses; commercial areas show retail buildings rather than residences.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation, with uniform light tones. They contrast with chaparral by lacking dense shrub vegetation and having sandy terrain; mountains show elevated rocky peaks; beaches show coastal sandy areas adjacent to water.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground, often covering large areas. They contrast with chaparral by having taller trees rather than low shrubs; meadows show open grassy areas without tree cover; wetlands show water-saturated ground rather than dense canopy.
freeway: Freeways are wide linear strips of paved concrete with multiple lanes, clear lane markings, and overpass intersections. They differ from overpasses by being ground-level continuous pavement rather than elevated bridge structures; runways are shorter and lack lane divisions; parking lots show vehicle storage rather than through-traffic corridors.
golf_course: Golf courses are large green areas with mowed fairways, lighter roughs, sand bunkers, and small water hazards, arranged in a connected network. They contrast with baseball diamonds by having fairways and bunkers rather than sports infields; meadows show natural grass without maintained features; tennis courts show rectangular sports courts.
ground_track_field: Ground track fields show oval running tracks with distinct lane markings, infield areas, and surrounding stands or facilities. They differ from stadiums by being track-focused athletic fields rather than large enclosed sports venues; baseball diamonds have diamond infields rather than oval tracks; railways show linear tracks rather than oval circuits.
harbor: Harbors show calm water areas enclosed by docks, piers, ships, and cranes, with visible boundaries and artificial shoreline modifications. They differ from ships by being entire waterfront facilities rather than individual vessels; parking lots have vehicles rather than ships; bridges are crossing structures rather than waterfront docks.
industrial_area: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from thermal power stations by having diverse factories rather than power generation structures; storage tanks show circular metallic containers rather than factory buildings; railway stations show tracks and passenger buildings.
intersection: Intersections show cross-shaped road junctions with clear pavement markings, turn lanes, and traffic islands. They contrast with roundabouts by having perpendicular crossing geometry rather than circular flow; freeways are continuous corridors rather than local junctions; mobile home parks show housing rather than road junctions.
island: Islands show land masses completely surrounded by water, with visible shorelines, vegetation or structures, and varied shapes. They differ from beaches by being entire landforms rather than shoreline strips; rivers show flowing water channels rather than land; sea ice shows frozen surfaces rather than solid land.
lake: Lakes appear as large, enclosed water bodies with smooth surfaces, irregular shorelines, and surrounding vegetation or terrain. They contrast with wetlands by having open water rather than water-saturated ground; sea ice shows frozen surfaces rather than open water; deserts show sand rather than water features.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees or shrubs, and no field lines. They contrast with forests by having open grass rather than dense tree canopy; rectangular farmland shows organized crop rows; golf courses have maintained fairways and bunkers rather than natural grass.
medium_residential: Medium residential shows moderately sized houses on medium lots with visible yards, driveways, and tree-lined streets. It differs from dense residential by having larger lots and more green space; mobile home parks show trailer units rather than houses; sparse residential shows wider spacing and more vegetation.
mobile_home_park: Mobile home parks show rows of small, narrow rectangular trailer units arranged in dense, uniform clusters with narrow access roads. They contrast with medium residential by having trailer units rather than permanent houses; dense residential shows permanent housing; baseball diamonds show sports fields rather than trailer units.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns, often with forested lower elevations. They contrast with deserts by having rocky peaks rather than sand dunes; snowberg shows snow-capped peaks rather than exposed rock; forests show tree cover without dramatic elevation.
overpass: Overpasses are elevated road segments supported by pillars, crossing above other roads or terrain, with visible ramps and shadows. They differ from freeways by being raised structures rather than ground-level pavement; bridges span over water rather than land; roundabouts show circular ground-level traffic patterns.
palace: Palaces show ornate, large-scale architecture with grand courtyards, gardens, and distinctive historical design features. They differ from churches by lacking religious spires and having palace-specific architecture; commercial areas show modern retail buildings; tennis courts show sports facilities rather than palace grounds.
parking_lot: Parking lots are flat, open areas with visible rows of parked vehicles in organized lanes with painted markings. They contrast with harbors by having vehicles rather than ships and water; industrial areas have buildings alongside parking; airports show runways and aircraft rather than just vehicle storage.
railway: Railways show linear track corridors with parallel metal rails, ties, and occasional signals or crossings, often with adjacent roads. They differ from railway stations by being track corridors rather than full station facilities with platforms; freeways show paved vehicle lanes rather than metal rails; bridges are elevated crossing structures.
railway_station: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots, often with linear rail lines. They contrast with industrial areas by having passenger platforms and buildings rather than factories; airports have runways and terminals rather than train tracks; roundabouts show circular road patterns.
rectangular_farmland: Rectangular farmland shows large agricultural fields with straight, geometric boundaries, uniform crop rows, and visible field edges. It differs from circular farmland by having rectangular geometry rather than pivot irrigation circles; terraces show stepped patterns on slopes; meadows show natural grass without crop rows.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation along banks. They contrast with lakes by being elongated flowing water rather than still enclosed water bodies; wetlands show water-saturated ground rather than flowing channels; bridges are structures spanning rivers.
roundabout: Roundabouts show circular road junctions with a central island, circulating lanes, and multiple approach roads. They differ from intersections by having circular flow rather than perpendicular crossing; tennis courts show rectangular sports courts; overpasses show elevated road structures rather than ground-level circles.
runway: Runways are long, straight, wide paved strips with clear parallel markings, end zones, and no intersecting cross streets. They contrast with freeways by being shorter with fewer lanes and aircraft markings; airports show terminal buildings alongside runways; parking lots show vehicle rows rather than runway pavement.
sea_ice: Sea ice appears as vast, white to light blue frozen surfaces with irregular cracks, floes, and variable ice thickness. It differs from lakes by being frozen rather than open water; snowberg shows snow on land rather than sea ice; beaches show sandy shorelines rather than frozen surfaces.
ship: Ships appear as large watercraft with distinct hulls, superstructures, decks, and masts, floating in harbors or open water. They differ from harbors by being individual vessels rather than entire waterfront facilities; sea ice shows frozen surfaces without vessels; islands show solid land rather than watercraft.
snowberg: Snowbergs show mountain peaks covered with white snow, with exposed rock faces, ridge lines, and shadow patterns. They differ from mountains by having snow cover rather than exposed rock; sea ice shows flat frozen surfaces rather than peaks; clouds show soft atmospheric formations rather than solid peaks.
sparse_residential: Sparse residential shows widely separated houses surrounded by large vegetated lots, with unpaved roads and low building density. It contrasts with medium residential by having larger lot sizes and more vegetation; churches show single religious buildings rather than residential neighborhoods; rectangular farmland shows agricultural fields rather than houses.
stadium: Stadiums show large sports or event venues with oval or rectangular shape, tiered seating, and surrounding parking lots. They contrast with ground track fields by having enclosed stands and larger scale; baseball diamonds have sports field markings rather than stands; palaces show ornate architecture rather than sports venues.
storage_tank: Storage tanks appear as large circular metallic containers with domed or flat roofs, arranged in industrial clusters. They differ from thermal power stations by being tank clusters rather than power generation facilities; industrial areas show factories rather than tank farms; circular farmland shows crop patterns rather than metallic containers.
tennis_court: Tennis courts are rectangular playing areas with visible nets, court lines, and smooth surfaces, often with surrounding fences. They differ from basketball courts by having nets and different court markings; mobile home parks show trailer units rather than sports courts; parking lots show vehicle rows rather than court surfaces.
terrace: Terraces show stepped agricultural or landscape patterns on slopes, with visible contour lines and retaining walls. They differ from rectangular farmland by having stepped geometry on slopes rather than flat field boundaries; circular farmland shows pivot irrigation patterns; stadiums show sports venue structures.
thermal_power_station: Thermal power stations show large cooling towers, steam plumes, industrial buildings, and extensive infrastructure. They differ from storage tanks by having cooling towers and power generation structures rather than tank clusters; industrial areas show diverse factories; commercial areas show retail buildings rather than power plants.
wetland: Wetlands show water-saturated ground with emergent vegetation, marshy textures, and irregular water channels or pools. They contrast with lakes by having marsh vegetation rather than open water; rivers show flowing channels rather than saturated ground; forests show dry land with tree cover.
